Off: mobile data only. On: follows Android routing; VPN exclusions and disconnections can expose traffic. SOCKS5 passwords do not encrypt the local link. Use USB or a trusted network.
Join the sender’s network first. Enter its shown IPv4 address and SOCKS5 password, which differs from the Wi-Fi password. IPv4 TCP/UDP only; compatibility testing is ongoing.
Allow nearby Wi-Fi devices (Android 13+) or location (Android 8–12) to create a Wi-Fi Direct group.
Enter the sender’s IPv4 address and a port from 1 to 65535.
Enter the SOCKS5 password shown on the sender.
Connect USB tethering or Wi-Fi and select an address first.
Start the receiver VPN before testing UDP.

Scan this inside DataNet Share on the receiving phone. It contains SOCKS5 and (when available) Wi-Fi passwords. Anyone who can see or photograph it can connect until you stop sharing. Automatic SOCKS5 passwords rotate with each session; manually reused passwords do not. A code can be scanned more than once.

If sender QR includes Wi-Fi credentials, scan it before joining the network. Credentials stay only in app memory; restarting sharing invalidates the old proxy password.
During a connection, network failures appear here even if the VPN stays connected. No private IPs, QR codes, or passwords are included. An empty record is not proof of Internet connectivity.
What would you like to do?
Scan a QR code to fill in the connection details.
Connection details imported. Join the sender Wi-Fi, then tap Start.
Optional. Default leaves name, password and frequency to Android. Custom group settings depend on the device; the connection may fail instead of using another band.
Blank = auto / forget saved · custom 8–63 ASCII (remembered)
Android 8–9: public Wi-Fi Direct API cannot set a custom network name, password or band. Android controls these settings.

Wi-Fi Direct encryption/security is managed by Android. This app cannot force WPA2 vs WPA3, Wi-Fi 4/5/6/7, radio channel, or WMM/QoS. The selected band is a request, not a guaranteed PHY mode. Your chosen Wi-Fi password is remembered with Android Keystore encryption until you clear it or uninstall the app.
Custom Wi-Fi Direct settings need Android 10 or later.
Could not securely remember the Wi-Fi password. No changes were applied; check device security storage and retry.
Saved Wi-Fi password could not be restored. Enter it again and start sharing to save it securely.

Custom Wi-Fi passwords are encrypted and remembered on this device. Stop sharing before changing settings, then start again to apply. Blank password removes the saved one and uses automatic generation.
Use validated Wi-Fi if mobile data is unavailable (optional)

Prefers cellular. If cellular is unavailable/unvalidated or a new connection fails, retries new connections over validated Wi-Fi. Requires a separate internet-capable Wi-Fi link; does not migrate existing streams or guarantee recovery. Ignored when Android default route is selected.
Release peer Wi-Fi if sender disappears (allow Android network fallback)

Optional: after three failed sender checks, close VPN and release the QR-requested local Wi-Fi. Android may then choose cellular or a previously saved Wi-Fi. This is not a kill switch and cannot join arbitrary networks.
Blank = random; custom 12–128 printable ASCII, no spaces
Use 12–128 printable ASCII characters without spaces for a custom SOCKS5 password.
After QR scan, request Wi-Fi connection and start receiver VPN (Android 10+)
Automatic Wi-Fi request requires Android 10+. Join Wi-Fi manually, then start VPN.
Nearby Wi-Fi permission denied. Connect manually in Android Wi-Fi settings.
Android Wi-Fi connection requested. Approve the system dialog to continue.
Android could not connect to the QR Wi-Fi. Join manually from Wi-Fi settings, then start VPN.
QR Wi-Fi was assigned an address, but the sender is unreachable. Check the live sender Wi-Fi name and QR code match, stop/restart sharing, or join manually in Android Wi-Fi settings.
Wi-Fi is now connected. Checking the sender’s local SOCKS5 port before starting VPN.

QR Wi-Fi was assigned an IPv4 address but the local sender proxy port is unreachable. Make sure this QR was generated by the currently active sender session. If it continues, join that Wi-Fi manually and start the receiver VPN.

Authenticated SOCKS5 IPs only. Not a list of all Wi-Fi devices. ↓ received from Internet, ↑ sent to Internet; bytes exclude protocol overhead. Totals reset when sharing stops.
